PAPERS.title: Long-term exposure to wildfire-related PM2.5 and overall survival of older patients with lung cancer: a retrospective, registry-based cohort study.
PAPERS.pm: 3-year moving average wildfire vs non-wildfire PM2.5, zip-code, model-derived
PAPERS.n: 414,016 SEER-Medicare patients aged 65+ with histologically confirmed lung cancer, 1,211,490 person-years, 2008-2019. Time-varying Cox. Per 1 ug/m3, wildfire PM2.5 carried HR 1.0782 (95% CI 1.0641-1.0924) for all-cause death against 1.0171 (1.0149-1.0192) for non-wildfire PM2.5 — a 4.6-fold difference in per-unit potency, the cleanest quantitative statement yet that wildfire smoke is not interchangeable with urban PM2.5 mass. The exposure contrast is the weakness: median wildfire PM2.5 was 0.28 ug/m3 (IQR 0.21-0.39) against 8.11 for non-wildfire, so the per-unit HR is extrapolated far outside the observed range and the per-SD estimates (1.0229 vs 1.0384) actually favour non-wildfire. Zip-code assignment with no residential history. Species-resolved, not mass-only, monitoring is the implication.

PAPERS.title: Ambient PM2.5 exposure and cancer incidence in Nigerian adults: A prospective cohort study.
PAPERS.pm: Hybrid satellite + land-use regression, 1 km annual PM2.5, PM10, NO2
PAPERS.n: 5,621 adults in Lagos, Kano and Rivers States, median follow-up 4.7 years, 25,418 person-years, 147 histopathologically confirmed incident cancers. Mean PM2.5 50.4 ug/m3, tenfold the WHO guideline. Each 10 ug/m3 gave HR 1.12 (95% CI 1.06-1.19) for all-cancer incidence; top versus bottom quartile HR 1.82 (1.29-2.57). Oxidative-stress and inflammatory biomarkers mediated 41.3% of the association. With 147 events across three states the site-specific claims for lung, breast and haematopoietic cancers rest on very small strata, and mediation from a biomarker subsample measured once cannot establish temporal ordering. The exposure surface is satellite-LUR with no in-country reference network to anchor it — precisely the gap a dense low-cost deployment would fill.

PAPERS.title: Environmental exposure and risk of death by suicide, attempted suicide and suicide ideation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM2.5 and PM10, short- and long-term contrasts pooled together
PAPERS.n: 45 studies screened, 29 pooled, covering air, noise, light and water pollution. Short-term PM2.5 gave OR 1.0139 (95% CI 1.0001-1.0279, 13 studies) and PM10 OR 1.0100 (1.0007-1.0195, 7 studies); long-term PM2.5 OR 1.5254 (1.1351-2.0481, 6 studies) and NO2 OR 1.3173 (1.0641-1.6308). The short-term PM2.5 lower bound sits at 1.0001 — significance is nominal. More seriously, the 38-fold gap between the short- and long-term PM2.5 point estimates is an artefact of pooling per-increment against high-versus-low categorical contrasts under one label; the two numbers are not on a common scale and should not be read as a dose-response. Newcastle-Ottawa only; no exposure-misclassification weighting.

PAPERS.title: Association between ambient fine particulate matter and hemorrhagic stroke in Yancheng, China.
PAPERS.pm: Station-average daily PM2.5, lag 0 to lag 01
PAPERS.n: Individual-level time-stratified case-crossover on 2,312 haemorrhagic stroke admissions across four Yancheng hospitals, 2022-2024, conditional logistic regression. Strongest at lag01: each 10 ug/m3 PM2.5 associated with a 3.24% increase in admissions (95% CI 0.55-6.00), with lag0 2.50% (0.11-4.95) and lag1 2.76% (0.32-5.27). The association survived adjustment for O3 but lost significance once SO2 or NO2 entered — which is the finding that matters, because it means the PM2.5 coefficient is not separable from co-emitted combustion products at this station density. Exposure is city-average from fixed monitors assigned to residence, so within-city gradients are unmeasured; a four-hospital catchment is not the full case population.

PAPERS.title: Ambient air pollutant mixtures in relation to sonographic endometrial receptivity parameters during the peri-implantation window: a clinic-based observational study.
PAPERS.pm: Monthly mean PM2.5, PM10, CO, NO2, SO2, O3 from a high-resolution reanalysis grid
PAPERS.n: 1,349 women across 14 cities in Liaoning, with quantile g-computation and BKMR on a six-pollutant mixture. A simultaneous one-quartile increase in the mixture was associated with 0.5 mm less endometrial thickness and 0.28 ml less volume; CO and O3 carried the largest weights, PM2.5 and PM10 did not dominate. No confidence intervals are reported for the mixture effects in the abstract, which for a BKMR result is a substantive omission. A 0.5 mm shift is at or below the reproducibility of transvaginal endometrial measurement, so the clinical meaning is unclear even if the association is real. Monthly gridded exposure with no personal or indoor component — the peri-implantation window is days, not months.

PAPERS.title: Gestational inhalation of nanoparticles disrupts placental zone structure and induces vascular placentation in rats.
PAPERS.pm: nano-TiO2 aerosol, 9.23 +/- 0.39 mg/m3 whole-body, as an ultrafine PM proxy
PAPERS.n: Pregnant Sprague Dawley rats exposed by whole-body inhalation to nano-TiO2 from gestational day 5 to 19, placentas harvested GD20 for histology. Placental weight and placental efficiency were unchanged, but decidua and labyrinth zone sizes fell, with compensatory increases in blood space number and maternal blood space area. The compensation is the interesting part: structural remodelling without a mass-level phenotype means placental weight is a poor screening endpoint for ultrafine exposure. The exposure concentration is roughly three orders of magnitude above ambient ultrafine mass and engineered TiO2 is a poor surrogate for combustion-derived ultrafines in surface chemistry, so this bounds mechanism, not risk. No litter-level statistics reported in the abstract.

PAPERS.title: Pneumococcal population structure influences the effects of air pollution on invasive disease risk in South Africa.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM2.5, lagged to 8 weeks, linked to serotype and lineage
PAPERS.n: 19 years of national surveillance, 59,017 invasive pneumococcal disease cases with 4,350 sequenced isolates, Bayesian spatiotemporal models. PM2.5 was positively associated with IPD, but the lag structure varied by serotype: only serotypes 4, 8 and 23F conferred immediate risk, and high prevalence of lineage GPSC21 (serotype 19F) shifted the population-level lag to immediate. Cumulative 8-week effects for moderate humidity and cold minimum temperature were +5% and +4%. No confidence interval is given for the headline pollution association, and with serotype-stratified lag models on a fixed case set the multiple-comparison surface is large. Still the first demonstration that pathogen genotype modifies an air-quality exposure-response — a genuine argument for pairing dense PM monitoring with pathogen surveillance.

PAPERS.title: Extreme Cold Events and Pediatric Asthma Outpatient Visits: The Modifying Role of Ambient Carbon Monoxide and Sulfur Dioxide.
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5 and PM10 as stratifying co-pollutants, not the exposure of interest
PAPERS.n: 62,167 paediatric asthma outpatient visits at one tertiary hospital, Nanjing, 2019-2024, quasi-Poisson DLNM over lag 0-14. Extreme cold events (>=2, 3 or 4 consecutive days at or below 4.5 C) showed no overall association, but cumulative RR reached 2.60 (95% CI 1.13-5.95) in the high-CO stratum and 3.41 (1.15-10.11) in the high-SO2 stratum. The intervals are very wide and the stratified estimates come from subsets of an already null main effect, so this is hypothesis-generating; PM2.5 and PM10 did not emerge as modifiers. Single-hospital catchment with city-average exposure. Relevant here mainly as a reminder that pollutant-by-meteorology interaction terms need far denser exposure data than one municipal station provides.

PAPERS.short: Narrative review, prenatal and early postnatal window
PAPERS.title: Early Life Exposure to Air Pollutants and Childhood Asthma.
PAPERS.pm: Prenatal and early postnatal ambient air pollutants, reviewed qualitatively
PAPERS.n: Narrative synthesis of recent cohort and mechanistic work linking prenatal and early postnatal air pollution to childhood asthma. Reports epigenetic modification in airway epithelium, a convergence point shared between tobacco smoke exposure and genetic asthma predisposition, new serum biomarkers of exposure, and a murine result in which asthma-predisposing information passes from exposed dam to offspring via NK cells. No pooled estimate, no effect size, no formal search strategy or inclusion criteria, so study selection is unauditable and the piece cannot be weighted against the systematic reviews in this window. Useful only as a pointer to the NK-cell transmission mechanism and to the biomarker candidates.

PAPERS.short: Partector 2 Pro vs SMPS and CPC, 4 filaments
PAPERS.title: Evaluation of the Partector 2 Pro for measuring ultrafine particles emitted from 3D printing.
PAPERS.pm: UFP number concentration and D10-D95 mobility diameter percentiles
PAPERS.n: Wind-tunnel comparison of the Partector 2 Pro diffusion-charging monitor against SMPS and CPC during controlled printing of PLA, PETG, TPU and nylon. Number concentration agreement was strong across all four materials: regression slopes 0.88-1.05, Pearson r > 0.96, mean deviations -9.6% to +6.2%, inside the +/-30% manufacturer specification. Sizing was systematically biased low (slopes 0.82-0.90), worst at the small end, -27.0% to +7.5% at D10 and -28.3% to -7.3% across D25-D75. That bias pattern matters for any distributed UFP network: the instrument is fit for concentration surveillance but its size distribution should not be used to infer deposition fraction. Wind tunnel only — no humidity or co-pollutant interference testing.

PAPERS.title: Exploring Environmental and Temporal Performances of Machine Learning Models for Calibration of a Low-Cost PM2.5 Sensor.
PAPERS.pm: Low-cost PM2.5 against reference, binned by temperature, RH, hour and month
PAPERS.n: Long-term co-location in Vishakhapatnam comparing Random Forest and XGBoost against linear regression, adding temperature, relative humidity, hour-of-day and month-of-year stepwise, plus a hybrid ensemble of the best models. The best single ML model cut RMSE 58% against the linear baseline and the hybrid reached 63%, meeting US EPA low-cost PM2.5 performance criteria. The contribution is the evaluation design rather than the models: performance is reported binned across environmental and temporal strata and across AQI categories, which exposes where a calibration degrades instead of hiding it in a pooled R-squared. No absolute RMSE in ug/m3 is given in the abstract, and single-site training leaves transferability untested — the same limitation flagged for the Sofia calibration-transfer work already in this corpus.

PAPERS.title: Non-Cumulative, Size-Specific Calibration of Low-Cost Particulate Matter Sensors Under Simulated Construction Drilling Events.
PAPERS.pm: Non-cumulative PM1, PM2.5, PM10 fractions under simulated concrete-slab drilling
PAPERS.n: Controlled laboratory evaluation of PMS5003 and Sniffer4D under simulated concrete-slab drilling, with six correction models (linear, polynomial, Random Forest, XGBoost, ANN, Kalman) fitted independently per size fraction. Random Forest and ANN performed best, R2 > 0.89 for PM1 and > 0.87 for PM2.5 at 50 s averaging. The premise is the useful part: reporting non-cumulative rather than cumulative bins, since cumulative output conflates fractions with different deposition and regulatory meaning. Against that, a single drilling source in a chamber produces a mineral-dust size distribution that will not transfer to combustion aerosol, and PM10 performance is not reported alongside the finer fractions. Crossref resolves this to the preprint DOI; the journal version was not separately indexed at harvest.

PAPERS.title: 14-Day PM2.5 and O3 Forecasting over Eastern China Using a Hybrid CNN-Transformer Architecture Driven by Multilevel Meteorological Fields.
PAPERS.pm: Gridded surface PM2.5 and O3 forecast from multilevel meteorology plus emissions
PAPERS.n: Hybrid CNN-Transformer forecasting O3 and PM2.5 14 days ahead across central-eastern China, combining multilevel regional meteorological fields with emission inventories. Relative R2 gains over baseline were 40% for O3 (0.58 to 0.81) and 18% for PM2.5 (0.44 to 0.52); adding 850 hPa fields helped O3 by 5% and emissions helped PM2.5 by 9.8%; 66-83% of O3 episodes were captured in the north. The honest reading is that PM2.5 skill remains poor — R2 0.52 at 14 days is not decision-grade, and the paper's own framing concedes O3 is the stronger case. No episode-capture rate is reported for PM2.5, which is the number a forecast user would act on. Gridded reanalysis truth, so station-scale error is not resolved.

PAPERS.title: A LASSO-based reduced-form CMAQ model for predicting ozone and PM2.5 responses to emission changes in South Korea.
PAPERS.pm: CMAQ-simulated surface PM2.5 and O3 response to sectoral emission perturbation
PAPERS.n: Reduced-form surrogate for CMAQ built with LASSO over 118 emission scenarios spanning seven sectors and 17 provincial regions, with an adaptive logit transform to respect concentration bounds. Trained on 100 simulations, tested on 18: mean RMSE 0.1 ppb for ozone and 0.1 ug/m3 for PM2.5 against the parent model. The selected sparse set of sector-region terms is the practical output, since it makes the emission-control design problem interpretable rather than a black box. Error is quoted against CMAQ, not against observations, so the surrogate inherits every CMAQ bias undiagnosed; 118 scenarios is thin for a 119-dimensional predictor space and no out-of-envelope extrapolation test is reported.

PAPERS.title: Predictive modelling of fine-mode combustion aerosol events near Indonesian coal-fired power plants using AE-filtered Himawari-8 satellite data.
PAPERS.pm: Himawari-8 AOD filtered by Angstrom exponent > 1.2 as a fine-mode combustion proxy
PAPERS.n: 41,119 daily Himawari-8 observations around 13 major Java coal plants, 2015-2025, with fine-mode combustion events defined as AE > 1.2 and AOD > 0.4 (8.52% of days). Suralaya had the highest mean AOD at 1.01 with 51.4% very-high-pollution days; Pacitan the lowest at 0.46. Random forest and XGBoost returned accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and AUC-ROC all exactly 1.000 — a perfect score on a binary target that is a deterministic threshold function of the two input variables, so the classifiers are relearning the labelling rule, not predicting anything. The 2026-2060 Monte Carlo projection built on that model is therefore uninterpretable. Column AOD without surface validation cannot separate plant plume from boundary-layer aerosol.

PAPERS.title: Spatiotemporal assessment of urban PM10 and population exposure using integrated satellite, meteorological, and socio-spatial data.
PAPERS.pm: MODIS-MAIAC AOD regressed onto station PM10, plus a socio-spatial exposure index
PAPERS.n: MODIS-MAIAC AOD combined with four ground stations and meteorology in a multiple regression for PM10 over Oradea, Romania, then folded with population density, built-form, NDVI and elevation into a composite exposure index. Cold-season maxima reached 41.8 ug/m3 with an annual mean near 20.5, above WHO and inside EU limits; 20.1% of the metropolitan population fell in high-predisposition areas. The AOD-PM10 relationship alone is weak (R = 0.28) and meteorology carries the model — which is the paper's own admission and the reason satellite-only exposure surfaces keep underperforming at city scale. Four stations cannot validate an intra-urban surface, and the composite index is unweighted and unvalidated against any measured personal exposure.

PAPERS.title: Source Apportionment of PM2.5 Oxidative Potential in metropolitan Melbourne: integrating PMF with multiple linear regression across three acellular assays.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 oxidative potential by DTT, AA and DCFH, regressed on PMF source contributions
PAPERS.n: Previously published PMF source contributions for metropolitan Melbourne linked by multiple linear regression to oxidative potential measured with three complementary acellular assays. Models explained 73-86% of OP variance. Combustion dominated OPv-DTT at 52-53% with biomass burning outweighing traffic; OPv-AA was driven by metal-rich sources including diesel at 20-22%; secondary nitrate contributed 28-33% and secondary sulphate 10% at the second site. The assay-dependent source ranking is the point — a single-assay OP metric would have given a different mitigation target — but it also means no one assay can stand as the health-relevant exposure. Reusing an earlier PMF solution propagates its rotational ambiguity, and no uncertainty is quoted on the source-resolved OP shares. First Southern Hemisphere estimate of its kind.

PAPERS.title: Unraveling decadal changes in PM2.5 sources and secondary aerosol formation drivers using integrated receptor model and machine learning.
PAPERS.pm: Speciated PM2.5 filter samples, PMF factors plus ML driver attribution
PAPERS.n: Eleven years of speciated PM2.5 sampling in Shenzhen with PMF source apportionment and machine-learning attribution of secondary formation drivers. Annual mean fell 37.7 to 17.3 ug/m3. Secondary sulphate was historically dominant and declined fastest; vehicle emissions became the largest single contributor after 2019; secondary nitrate barely moved and is now the binding constraint. ML indicated that NOx and VOC reductions drove nitrate and SOA declines but rising atmospheric oxidation capacity offset them, while sulphate was controlled by oxidation and regional transport more than local SO2. Attribution of a decadal trend to oxidation capacity from a correlational ML model over a single site cannot exclude meteorological confounding; no uncertainty bounds on the PMF factor time series.

PAPERS.title: Carbonaceous Composition and Multi-Wavelength Optical Properties of Particulate Matter in Lahore, Pakistan.
PAPERS.pm: Gravimetric PM2.5, OC/EC, five-wavelength absorption (375-850 nm) by MWAA
PAPERS.n: Six-week urban campaign in Lahore, 30 quartz filters collected, 25 usable for gravimetry and optics and only the first 15 analysed for OC/EC. PM2.5 ranged 40-417 ug/m3, mean 137 +/- 84. Organic carbon was 76.6% of total carbon, elemental carbon 23.4%. Mean absorption Angstrom exponent was 1.17 +/- 0.30, with 56% of samples in 1.0-1.5, 32% below 1.0 and 12% above 1.5. The authors are appropriately careful that AAE intervals give spectral description, not source attribution. Fifteen OC/EC filters over six weeks in one pre-monsoon season cannot characterise Lahore's annual cycle, and without a co-located reference the gravimetric series has no traceability. Directly relevant to optical low-cost sensors, whose response depends on exactly this absorption behaviour.

PAPERS.title: Surface-Based Temperature Inversions Climatology Across China from Microwave Radiometer Network and Their Relationship to PM2.5 Pollution.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 at hotspot stations against hourly MWR-derived inversion and mixing-layer metrics
PAPERS.n: Hourly microwave-radiometer temperature profiles from 33 mainland Chinese stations over 2024-2025, validated against radiosondes at 25 sites, used to build a surface-based inversion climatology and relate it to PM2.5. Winter SBI occurrence was 39.2% against 12.1% in summer, with a northwest-to-southeast gradient peaking in the Tarim Basin and Hexi Corridor. SHAP and Spearman analysis put boundary-layer variables in the top predictor tier at monthly and daily scale, with effective mixing-layer height third among all hourly predictors in every season. Two years is short for a climatology and the MWR network is sparse relative to the terrain it spans; SHAP importance on correlated meteorological predictors does not establish the causal pathway it is read as establishing.

PAPERS.title: Relationships Between PM2.5 and Its Precursor Gases in Agricultural Areas of South Korea Using a Loading-Rate-Based Analysis.
PAPERS.pm: Hourly PM2.5 and NH3, NO2, SO2, expressed as concentration and as wind-scaled loading rate
PAPERS.n: 547 days of hourly data from eight agricultural monitoring sites, comparing concentration-based with loading-rate-based interpretation, where loading rate is concentration scaled by a wind-speed-derived air exchange rate. Concentration correlations among PM2.5 and NH3, NO2 and SO2 were weak and inconsistent; loading-rate correlations were strong and uniform at r >= 0.816, and diurnal shape flipped from bimodal to unimodal. The authors concede the improvement may simply reflect the shared wind-speed term — which it almost certainly does, since dividing every series by the same quantity induces correlation. Presented here as a method to treat with suspicion rather than adopt: any dense open-field network normalising by a common meteorological variable will manufacture the same result.

PAPERS.title: Indoor Air Protection Under Extreme Air Pollution Risk: Evidence From a Sandstorm in China.
PAPERS.pm: Sandstorm-driven outdoor PM episode as an exogenous shock; no PM measured directly
PAPERS.n: Difference-in-differences on Baidu search intensity for air purifiers and indoor air quality information around China's most intense sandstorm in a decade (early 2021), treating the event as an exogenous hazard. Affected regions showed roughly 18% higher search intensity than unaffected ones, rising to about 33% in historically cleaner areas and about 200% where baseline purifier sales were lowest. The gradient is the useful result: protective response scales inversely with prior exposure experience and prior equipment stock. Search volume is a proxy for intent, not for purchase, use, or any realised reduction in indoor PM2.5 — no concentration data enter the study at all. Regional treatment assignment with no individual exposure makes the effect ecological throughout.
